output.myth: Vanu was a skua who would not fish for herself. She sat on the wind above the water and waited for the gulls to dive, and when they came up with their silver in their beaks she stooped on them, hooked her bill in their throats, and took the fish. The gulls cried. They have been crying ever since, and that is why you hear them at the harbour mouth in the evening. Tavo the Gale heard them and laughed until the sea came up over the rocks. Then he took Vanu by the tail and threw her high, and she has been hanging in the north since, borrowed wings and all. Hesk keeps count of what she took. Aun once asked her why, and she said, "Because you cut the string and nobody gave it back." Aun said nothing. Mind your fish when the skua is over the water.
output.verse:
Skua stoops and takes
Gulls cry from the harbour wall
Borrowed wings, unpaid.
